guard: Interactive actor re-grants and revokes retire the current lifecycle through the auth authority plane before rotating or deleting the row, and the legacy static control is a real lifecycle-bound credential.
why: A copied elevated-view bearer must die across a whole-row authorization update. The CLI therefore retires the current lifecycle through the capability-gated loopback auth route before grantActor rotates the row; issuance never performs takeover as a side effect.
Revoke uses the same retirement before deleting the row, so a later grant can create a real successor instead of colliding with an active predecessor head.
The old-static refusal controls must still use a credential shape current core would mint; a pre-lifecycle agent stub can fail before the user-mode guard and falsely confirm the policy.

A rotated row can remain unused while the authority head still names its retired predecessor. A second re-grant must treat that current uid as not started rather than conflict with a lifecycle that is already terminal.
The retirement endpoint is a same-user loopback operator surface: browser origins and callers without the per-start capability must be rejected before any ledger or authority state is touched.
The request shape and current ledger row bind the operation to one exact actor incarnation. Unknown fields or a non-current lifecycle uid must not turn retirement into a takeover primitive.
If the daemon cannot confirm retirement, re-grant must fail before grantActor writes anything. Treating a transport failure as a no-op would rotate the row without fencing the predecessor.
